bullets.section: New podcast experiment I’m excited about
bullets.title: Behind-The-Scenes Live Session with Jake Becraft
bullets.note:
The most fascinating conversations I have are often behind closed doors: weekly jam sessions with [portfolio](https://tim.blog/portfolio/) startup founders. I’ve long assumed them too confidential to share, but this episode is my first exception. It’s a fun one, as there are clear before-and-after results.  
​  
This early-stage brainstorming session helped refine talking points that ended up in the Oval Office two months later.  
​  
My guest is [Jake Becraft](https://x.com/DrSynbio), CEO and co-founder of [Strand Therapeutics](https://www.strandtx.com/), which is building one of the most advanced programmable genetic medicine platforms in biotech. In this conversation, you’ll learn a lot about the future of medicine, how modern biotech works (or doesn’t), and much more.  
​  
Find Jake on X at [@DrSynbio](https://x.com/DrSynbio) and learn more at [strandtx.com](http://strandtx.com).  
​  
I’m tentatively calling this potential series “Tim’s Founder Kitchen,” but I’d love other suggestions! Please give it a listen, and let me know what you think on X ([@tferriss](https://x.com/tferriss)). Open to all recommendations for improvement.  
​  
Available on [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/868-tims-founder-kitchen-from-brainstorm-to-the/id863897795?i=1000770838211), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/04EV7D2yhOJtKxuqyoC6TP?si=IoqB_IODQTiss2QuRD-Wtw&nd=1&dlsi=a9116c112473462f), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mZ-vJ6kDRD0), or wherever you get your podcasts.

bullets.section: How I’m finally getting in more Zone 2 cardio
bullets.title: M3i Studio Indoor Bike | Keiser
bullets.note:
I’ve tried a lot of stationary bikes, including very fancy indoor trainers, for getting in Zone 2 cardio and VO2 max training. I hate nearly all of them. This M3i is \*not\* fancy, but it does allow me to elevate the handlebars enough so that (1) I’m not bumping my thighs into my stomach like a one-hour Heimlich maneuver, and (2) it doesn’t make my low back incredibly grumpy. The controls are simple, it’s durable, I don’t use an app with it, and, so far, it’s the only indoor bike that I’ve used consistently. And more good news: it’s found in a lot of commercial gyms.  
​**​  
​**Google AI overview: “The Keiser M3i Indoor Bike is highly acclaimed by users and reviewers, often considered one of the best, most durable, and smoothest commercial-grade spin bikes for home use. Key praise centers on its whisper-quiet magnetic resistance, excellent durability, and accurate power data.”
